subject: Clarify indemnity split and evidence routing for Order Form
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: J. Patel <j.patel@acme-procure.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T16:15:00Z
Subject: Order Form redlines — indemnity and evidence routing

Olga,

Thanks for the draft Order Form. Our legal team attached redlines that narrow Redwood's indemnity for third-party IP claims — specifically they want: 
- a requirement that Acme reasonably mitigate and lead any takedown/notice responses;
- a rebuttable presumption that customer-created prompts/outputs are handled by the customer (i.e., carveout for user-provided content);
- tighter notice requirements (7 days), and clear evidence we expect from Redwood to validate claims.

We attached ACME_OrderForm_Redlines_v2.pdf. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the proposed defend-vs-reimburse split, and who on your side would be the evidence owner in an infringement claim?

Also copying procurement (J) to start the commercial thread.

Thanks,
Liam O'Neill
Sr. Contracts Manager
Acme Corp

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_Redlines_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-10T09:04:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Order Form redlines — indemnity and evidence routing

Kim / Ben — forwarding Acme's redlines. High-level asks from Acme: 7-day notice window, customer carveout for prompt-derived outputs, and request that Acme leads mitigation and Redwood provides evidence.

Pointing this at legal (Kim) for a quick read, and putting Ben on the loop for ops implications (evidence timelines, logs). Questions we need to answer before replying to Acme: 

- Can we accept a 7-day notice SLA? (our current standard is 14 days; shorter window increases risk of missing forensic artifacts)
- Who owns collection of evidence (model traces, KV cache, request payloads)? Ops prefers Redwood to own runtime artifacts but we can commit to handing a curated evidence bundle within X days.
- Carveouts: Acme wants user-generated prompt/output carveout. Legal: is a narrow carveout (explicit user-supplied prompts and customer-uploaded data only) acceptable?
- Defense control: Acme's redline leans to customer-led mitigation with Redwood providing support. Legal: do we insist on control for third-party claims or can we offer defend-vs-reimburse with a cooperation clause?

Please reply with the recommended position and author of the response. If it helps, I can propose a concrete compromise to send back (e.g., 10-day notice, Redwood delivers a forensic bundle within 7 business days after notice, defend-vs-reimburse with Redwood retaining right to take control if litigation is likely).

Olga Petrov
Sr. Contracts Ops, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Redlines_summary_olga_comments.txt (text)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-10T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form redlines — indemnity and evidence routing

Thanks for the ping, Olga. Read through Acme's redlines — concise suggested positions below. Goal: preserve our defend/control stance for third-party IP claims but be pragmatic to close the commercial.

Recommended legal positions (short):
- Notice window: propose 10 business days (not calendar) as a compromise. We need enough time to snapshot runtime state and KV cache; shorter windows create operational impossibility.
- Evidence owner: Redwood will be the custodian of runtime artifacts. We'll commit to producing a curated evidence bundle (request payloads, token-level logs, model name & version, sampling seed where available) within 7 business days after acceptably-scoped notice. We should exclude PII redaction process details in the bundle unless requested under a lawful process.
- Carveout: accept a narrow user-content carveout limited to explicit customer uploads and clearly labeled user prompts. Reject a broad carveout for all "prompt-derived outputs" — that would swallow most claims.
- Defense control: offer defend-vs-reimburse for non-software claims but retain right to assume defense (with counsel approval) if Redwood determines the claim could materially impact other customers or relates to core model architecture. Provide a coordination clause requiring cooperation and mutual consent for settlements that materially affect the other party.

Operational ask for Ben: confirm feasibility of delivering the forensic bundle within 7 business days and whether we need a secure transfer process / legal hold to be included in the order form. If Ben can't meet 7 business days, propose an alternative SLA.

If Ops confirms, Olga please send the above as a counterproposal to Acme (I can draft the legal redline language for the MSA/Order Form). If they push back on defend control we can present examples where customer-led defense led to poor outcomes and offer insurance/escrow alternatives as a trade.

Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@acme.com>, J. Patel <j.patel@acme-procure.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-11T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — indemnity and evidence routing

Liam / J.,

Thanks for the redlines and the clear ask. We've reviewed internally and propose the following compromise to keep the deal moving: 

1) Notice window: 10 business days (from receipt of a written notice). This balances your need for quick action with our need to preserve runtime artifacts for analysis.

2) Evidence & collection: Redwood will act as custodian of runtime artifacts. Upon a valid notice, Redwood will produce a curated evidence bundle (request payloads, model name/version, token-level logs to the extent retained, and cross-request correlation keys) within 7 business days. We will exclude information that is privileged or subject to PII redaction except where legally required.

3) Carveout: we accept a narrow carveout for customer-uploaded content and explicitly provided prompts. We cannot agree to a broad carveout that covers any output that might be traced to a prompt; that would eliminate necessary protections.

4) Defense: Redwood prefers to retain the right to assume defense for third-party IP claims affecting our core model or platform. However, to close this order swiftly we can offer a defend-vs-reimburse solution for customer-content-specific claims, with a coordination clause requiring mutual consent for settlements that impact the other party.

If that sounds reasonable I can circulate a redlined Order Form that implements these points and set a 30-minute call tomorrow to talk through any remaining items.

Proposed call times: 2026-08-11 14:00 PST / 17:00 EST / 21:00 UTC. Please tell us which works.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Contracts Ops, Redwood Inference
